why: issue 2148 (2026-10-30) — upstream `rclcpp::Client::take_response(response, request_header)`, on the class that can perform it: the poll client owns its `RmwServiceClient`, the dispatch `rclcpp::Client<S>` hands every reply to its handler in the arena. Takes the next reply WITH its `rmw_request_id_t`, through `nros_cpp_service_client_take_response_with_request_id`, filled from the backend's `take_response_with_info` (issue 2136): the sequence number the request went out under always, this client's request-writer GUID where the backend reports one (zenoh, Cyclone DDS; XRCE-DDS reports none, the Agent owns the request writer), all zero where it does not. As upstream's it takes WHATEVER reply is next and touches no pending future, so a caller mixing it with `async_send_request` correlates on the header, as upstream's does. DIVERGENCE in the return: upstream returns `bool` and throws on a failed take; RFC-0018 forbids exceptions, so `Result` distinguishes `TryAgain` (nothing waiting) from a failure, and its explicit `operator bool` keeps `if (client->take_response(resp, header))` compiling. Test: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/client_take_response_runtime.cpp` (stub, `just check cpp`); live: `interop_e2e::interop::case_12_zenoh_service_response_header_cpp` against a stock `rmw_zenoh_cpp` server.
